title_en: He Lihong v. China Life Insurance Company Limited, Foshan Shunde Branch and China Life Insurance Company Limited, Foshan Branch — dispute over insurance contract
ruling_gist_en: I. Due to the special nature of insurance contracts, the parties to the contract shall act with the utmost good faith. The policyholder's fulfillment of the duty of truthful disclosure in accordance with law is an important aspect of the utmost good faith. Pursuant to Article 17 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Insurance Law), before entering into an insurance contract, the policyholder shall truthfully answer the insurer's inquiries regarding the insured subject matter or the insured person, and truthfully disclose important matters that affect the insurer's correct decision on whether to underwrite and how to set underwriting conditions and premium rates. If the policyholder intentionally conceals facts and fails to perform the duty of truthful disclosure, or negligently fails to perform the duty of truthful disclosure to an extent sufficient to affect the insurer's decision on whether to agree to underwrite or to increase the premium rate, the insurer shall have the right to rescind the insurance contract and shall not be liable for compensation or payment of insurance benefits for insured events occurring before the rescission of the insurance contract.

full_text_en:
He Lihong v. China Life Insurance Co., Ltd., Foshan Shunde Sub-branch, and China Life Insurance Co., Ltd., Foshan Branch — dispute over an insurance contract

Ruling Summary

I. Given the special nature of an insurance contract, the parties to the contract shall act in good faith to the maximum extent. The policyholder's fulfillment of the duty of truthful disclosure according to law is an important aspect of acting in good faith to the maximum extent. Pursuant to Article 17 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Insurance Law), before concluding an insurance contract, the policyholder shall truthfully answer the insurer's inquiries concerning the subject matter insured or the insured, and shall truthfully disclose important matters that affect the insurer's correct decision on whether to accept the insurance and how to set the insurance conditions and premium rates. If the policyholder intentionally conceals facts or fails to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure, or if due to negligence the policyholder fails to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure, to the extent that it is sufficient to affect the insurer's decision on whether to agree to underwrite the insurance or to increase the premium rate, the insurer shall have the right to rescind the insurance contract, and shall not be liable for compensation or payment of insurance benefits for any insurance accident occurring prior to the rescission of the insurance contract.

II. If the insurer, while knowing that the policyholder has failed to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure, does not further require the policyholder to make truthful disclosure but instead enters into the insurance contract with the policyholder, it shall be deemed to have voluntarily waived its right of defense, constituting a legally binding waiver. Therefore, it shall no longer have the right to rescind the insurance contract on the ground that the policyholder violated the duty of truthful disclosure, and shall strictly assume insurance liability in accordance with the terms of the insurance contract.

Plaintiff: He Lihong, female, 40 years old, residing at Yang'e Zhongyi Street, Lunjiao Town, Shunde District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province.

Defendant: China Life Insurance Co., Ltd., Foshan Shunde Sub-branch, domiciled at Jianhai North Road, Daliang Street Office, Shunde District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province.

Person in Charge: Huang Shaoguang, General Manager of the Sub-branch.

Defendant: China Life Insurance Co., Ltd., Foshan Branch, domiciled at Jihua Fifth Road, Chancheng District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province.

Person in Charge: Huang Liangjing, General Manager of the Branch.

The plaintiff, He Lihong, filed a lawsuit with the People's Court of Shunde District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province, against the defendants, China Life Insurance Co., Ltd., Foshan Shunde Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Shunde Sub-branch) and China Life Insurance Co., Ltd., Foshan Branch (hereinafter referred to as Foshan Branch), over a dispute concerning an insurance contract.

The plaintiff, He Lihong, alleged: Prior to his death, the policyholder Huang Guoji (the plaintiff's husband) entered into two insurance contracts with Yan Xiaohui, a salesperson of the Lunjiao Office affiliated with the defendant Shunde Sub-branch, including: (1) a "Personal Accident Comprehensive Insurance Contract" concluded on March 16, 2004, with an insurance amount of RMB 310,000 and a premium of RMB 390; (2) a "Xianghe Term Life Insurance Contract" concluded on March 25, 2004, with an insurance amount of RMB 200,000 and a premium of RMB 594. The insured under both insurance contracts was Huang Guoji, and the beneficiary was the plaintiff. On July 7, 2004, Huang Guoji died accidentally. According to the forensic examination report issued by the Forensic Medical Examination Center of Sun Yat-sen University, Huang Guoji's death was consistent with cardiopulmonary rupture and hemorrhagic shock caused by a traffic accident. The plaintiff believed that this accident met the conditions for compensation under the insurance contracts. On August 27, 2004, the plaintiff submitted an insurance claim to the defendants, Shunde Sub-branch and Foshan Branch, along with relevant written materials. After accepting the claim request, the two defendants unreasonably suspected that the plaintiff had fabricated the insurance accident, refused to perform their compensation obligations, and seriously infringed upon the plaintiff's lawful rights and interests. Therefore, the plaintiff requested the court to order the two defendants to immediately pay the plaintiff insurance benefits of RMB 500,000 plus interest (calculated from the date of filing the lawsuit to the date of repayment at the similar loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China), and to bear the litigation costs of this case.

The defendants, Shunde Sub-branch and Foshan Branch, argued: The defendants had sufficient reasons to deny the claim. 1. The policyholder, Huang Guoji, violated the duty of truthful disclosure. On March 8, 2004, Huang Guoji submitted two "Individual Insurance Application Forms" to apply for the defendants' "Xianghe Term Life Insurance" and "Personal Accident Comprehensive Insurance," and clearly stated in the application forms that he was not currently participating in or applying for any other personal insurance. However, in fact, Huang Guoji had multiple insurance records in the days before and after this date, including: purchasing three "Ankang Ruyika Insurance" policies from China Pacific Life Insurance Co., Ltd., Shunde Sub-branch on February 29, 2004, and March 2, 2004, with a total insurance amount of RMB 288,000; purchasing five "Ruyika Insurance" policies from Ping An Life Insurance Co. of China, Ltd. on March 1, 2004, with an insurance amount of RMB 150,000; purchasing one "Yukuai Personal Accident Insurance" policy from Tianan Insurance Co., Ltd., Shunde Branch on March 4, 2004, with an insurance amount of RMB 1,000,000; and purchasing three "Duobaotong Jixiang Card" policies from New China Life Insurance Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch on March 5, 2004, and March 9, 2004, with an insurance amount of RMB 300,000. The total insurance amount of the above policies was RMB 1,738,000. In addition, Huang Guoji falsely claimed to be a business owner when applying for insurance. In the two "Individual Insurance Application Forms" involved, Huang Guoji stated that his work unit was "Lunjiao Construction and Water and Electricity Installation Team" and his position was "Person in Charge," with occupation code "070121" and occupation class "Level 1." In the "High Amount Financial Questionnaire," he stated that his work unit was "Shunji Water and Electricity Decoration" and his position was "General Management." However, neither "Lunjiao Construction and Water and Electricity Installation Team" nor "Shunji Water and Electricity Decoration" had business registration. Therefore, it could be determined that Huang Guoji had no work unit at the time and was self-employed, with occupation code "210302." 2. Huang Guoji's violation of the duty of truthful disclosure was intentional. Huang Guoji and the beneficiary of the involved insurance, the plaintiff He Lihong, had previously been salespersons of Taikang Life Insurance Co., Ltd. and had received professional training on insurance-related knowledge. They should have known the provisions of the Insurance Law regarding the policyholder's duty of truthful disclosure. Moreover, within one week before applying for the insurance involved, they had applied for personal accident insurance from four different insurance companies, paying premiums of several thousand yuan. It was impossible for them not to know that they were already participating in or applying for other personal insurance. Therefore, it could be inferred that Huang Guoji intentionally failed to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure. 3. Huang Guoji's intentional failure to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure seriously affected the insurer's underwriting work and determination of insurance premiums, ultimately leading the insurer to make an untrue expression of intent. Pursuant to Article 17 of the Insurance Law, the insurer had the right to rescind the insurance contract and was not obligated to pay insurance benefits. 4. Both insurance policies involved were issued by Foshan Branch, and the invoices were also issued by Foshan Branch. Therefore, the parties to the insurance contracts involved were Huang Guoji and Foshan Branch. Shunde Sub-branch was not a party to the insurance contracts involved, was not a proper defendant in this case, and should not bear legal liability.

In response to the defense arguments of the defendants, Shunde Sub-branch and Foshan Branch, the plaintiff He Lihong supplemented the following opinions: It was true that the policyholder Huang Guoji had purchased personal insurance from multiple insurance companies. However, when purchasing the "Personal Accident Comprehensive Insurance" involved, Huang Guoji did not answer item 11 of the disclosure matters in the application form (i.e., whether he was currently participating in or applying for any other personal insurance) and thus did not violate the duty of truthful disclosure. When purchasing the "Xianghe Term Life Insurance" involved, although Huang Guoji did not disclose the matter of applying for insurance from other insurance companies, Huang Guoji failed to fulfill the duty of disclosure due to negligence. Only when the undisclosed major matter seriously affects the occurrence of the insured accident does the insurer have the right to deny compensation for the insured accident occurring before the rescission of the insurance contract. The occurrence of the insured accident involved was not caused by the major matter undisclosed by the policyholder. Therefore, it could be determined that the policyholder's failure to fulfill the duty of disclosure did not have a "serious impact" on the occurrence of the insured accident involved. Accordingly, the insurer could not rescind the insurance contract or refuse to bear insurance liability on this ground.

After the court organized the parties to exchange evidence in accordance with the law and held a public hearing, the People's Court of Shunde District, Foshan City, found the following facts:

The defendant Shunde Sub-branch was a subordinate branch of the defendant Foshan Branch. On March 8, 2004, Huang Guoji and the plaintiff He Lihong went together to the Lunjiao Office, a subordinate of Shunde Sub-branch, to apply for "Xianghe Term Life Insurance" with an insurance amount of RMB 200,000 (application form No. 1001440200964435) and "Personal Accident Comprehensive Insurance" with an insurance amount of RMB 310,000 (application form No. 1001440200731249). The applicant and insured for both insurance policies was Huang Guoji, and the beneficiary was He Lihong. In the insurance application forms, Huang Guoji filled in the work unit as "Lunjiao Construction and Water and Electricity Installation Team," occupation as "Person in Charge," occupation code as "070121," and average annual income as "RMB 50,000." For item 11 of the disclosure matters in Part 3 of the insurance application form, i.e., "A. Are you currently participating in or applying for any other personal insurance? If yes, please inform the underwriting company, name of insurance type, insurance amount, and effective date of the policy; B. Has any insurance company ever rescinded a contract with you or delayed, refused, or imposed additional conditions on your application for personal insurance in the past two years; C. Have you ever claimed against an insurance company in the past," Huang Guoji answered "No" in insurance application form No. 1001440200964435, but left it blank in insurance application form No. 1001440200731249.

On March 15, 2004, the defendant Foshan Branch issued to Huang Guoji a "Personal Accident Comprehensive Insurance Contract" with contract number 2004-441406-D31-58001682-5, with an insurance amount of RMB 310,000 (including personal accident insurance of RMB 300,000 and accidental medical insurance of RMB 10,000), a premium of RMB 390, and an effective date of March 16, 2004. On the same day, Huang Guoji paid the premium of RMB 390 to Foshan Branch. On March 24, 2004, Foshan Branch issued to Huang Guoji a "Xianghe Term Life Insurance Contract" with contract number 2004-441406-S51-00007131-0, with an insurance amount of RMB 200,000, a premium of RMB 594, and an effective date of March 25, 2004. On the same day, Huang Guoji paid the premium of RMB 594 to Foshan Branch.

On July 7, 2004, Huang Guoji died accidentally. The forensic examination report from the Forensic Medical Examination Center of Sun Yat-sen University determined that Huang Guoji's death was consistent with cardiopulmonary rupture and hemorrhagic shock caused by a traffic accident. On August 27, 2004, the plaintiff He Lihong submitted an insurance claim to the defendant Foshan Branch along with relevant written materials. However, Foshan Branch refused to pay, citing reasons such as that the policyholder Huang Guoji had intentionally violated the duty of truthful disclosure and that the insurer had the right to rescind the contract. On August 31, 2004, Foshan Branch and the defendant Shunde Sub-branch reported to the Shunde Branch of the Foshan Municipal Public Security Bureau, alleging that He Lihong was suspected of insurance fraud. On November 15, 2004, the Shunde Branch of the Foshan Municipal Public Security Bureau issued a notice of non-filing of the case.

Additional facts found: Huang Guoji purchased three "Ankang Ruyika Insurance" policies from China Pacific Life Insurance Co., Ltd., Shunde Sub-branch on February 29, 2004, and March 2, 2004, with a total insurance amount of RMB 288,000; purchased five "Ruyika Insurance" policies from Ping An Life Insurance Co. of China, Ltd. on March 1, 2004, with an insurance amount of RMB 150,000; purchased one "Yukuai Personal Accident Insurance" policy from Tianan Insurance Co., Ltd., Shunde Branch on March 4, 2004, with an insurance amount of RMB 1,000,000; and purchased three "Duobaotong Jixiang Card" policies from New China Life Insurance Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch on March 5, 2004, and March 9, 2004, with an insurance amount of RMB 300,000. The total insurance amount of the above policies was RMB 1,738,000.

Huang Guoji joined Taikang Life Insurance Co., Ltd. on September 16, 2003, working as a part-time agent for personal life insurance business, and resigned on January 2, 2004. The plaintiff He Lihong joined Taikang Life Insurance Co., Ltd. on September 4, 2003, working as a part-time agent for personal life insurance business, and resigned on February 2, 2004.

The above facts are confirmed by the various evidence submitted by the parties, which has been exchanged and authenticated in accordance with the law, and are sufficient for determination.

The issues in dispute at first instance in this case were: 1. Whether Huang Guoji intentionally violated the duty of truthful disclosure when applying for the insurance involved; 2. Whether the defendants Foshan Branch and Shunde Sub-branch should bear insurance liability.

The People's Court of Shunde District, Foshan City, held at first instance:

I. On the issue of whether the policyholder Huang Guoji intentionally violated the duty of truthful disclosure when applying for the insurance involved.

Given the special nature of an insurance contract, the parties to the contract shall act in good faith to the maximum extent. The policyholder's fulfillment of the duty of truthful disclosure according to law is an important aspect of acting in good faith to the maximum extent. Article 17 of the Insurance Law provides: "When concluding an insurance contract, the insurer shall explain the terms and conditions of the insurance contract to the applicant, and may make inquiries concerning the subject matter insured or the insured, and the applicant shall truthfully answer such inquiries. If the applicant intentionally conceals facts and fails to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure, or if due to negligence the applicant fails to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure, to the extent that it is sufficient to affect the insurer's decision on whether to agree to underwrite the insurance or to increase the premium rate, the insurer shall have the right to rescind the insurance contract. If the applicant intentionally fails to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure, the insurer shall not be liable for compensation or payment of insurance benefits for any insured accident occurring prior to the rescission of the insurance contract, and shall not return the premiums. If the applicant fails to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure due to negligence, and such failure has a serious impact on the occurrence of the insured accident, the insurer shall not be liable for compensation or payment of insurance benefits for any insured accident occurring prior to the rescission of the insurance contract, but may return the premiums. An insured accident refers to an accident falling within the scope of insurance liability under the insurance contract." Accordingly, the duty of truthful disclosure is a basic obligation that the policyholder must fulfill when concluding an insurance contract. Whether the policyholder provides truthful information concerning the subject matter insured or the insured directly affects the insurer's assessment and evaluation of underwriting risk and its decision on whether to underwrite, as well as the insurer's choice of premium rates. Therefore, before concluding an insurance contract, the policyholder shall truthfully answer the insurer's inquiries concerning the subject matter insured or the insured, and shall truthfully disclose important matters that affect the insurer's decision on whether to accept the insurance and how to set the insurance conditions and premium rates.

Based on the facts of this case, it can be determined that the policyholder Huang Guoji intentionally violated the duty of truthful disclosure when applying for the insurance involved with respect to the issue of whether he had applied for the same type of insurance from multiple insurance companies.

First, with respect to truthfully disclosing his occupation, the policyholder need only truthfully describe his work situation to fulfill the relevant duty of truthful disclosure. How to characterize the policyholder's work into a specific occupation, occupation class, and occupation code should be determined by the insurer based on the policyholder's circumstances. Requiring the policyholder to accurately define the occupation class and code himself would exceed the capability of an ordinary policyholder. In this case, when applying for the insurance involved, the policyholder Huang Guoji stated that he was engaged in water and electricity installation work. Relevant evidence also confirmed that Huang Guoji indeed had qualifications for water and electricity installation and actually engaged in such work. Whether Huang Guoji had also worked part-time as an insurance company salesperson does not affect the truthfulness of the above statement regarding his occupation. Therefore, it can be determined that Huang Guoji had fulfilled the duty of truthful disclosure with respect to his occupation.

Second, the policyholder Huang Guoji purchased "Xianghe Term Life Insurance" and "Personal Accident Comprehensive Insurance" from the defendant Foshan Branch, entering into two insurance contracts. When purchasing the "Xianghe Term Life Insurance," Huang Guoji answered "No" to all three inquiries in item 11 of Part 3 of the application form regarding insurance records: "A. Are you currently participating in or applying for any other personal insurance? If yes, please inform the underwriting company, name of insurance type, insurance amount, and effective date of the policy; B. Has any insurance company ever rescinded a contract with you or delayed, refused, or imposed additional conditions on your application for personal insurance in the past two years; C. Have you ever claimed against an insurance company in the past." When Huang Guoji applied for the "Personal Accident Comprehensive Insurance" from Foshan Branch, he neither answered "Yes" nor "No" to item 11 regarding whether he had applied for insurance from multiple insurance companies; that is, he left it unanswered. However, according to the facts of this case, Huang Guoji purchased multiple personal insurance policies from several insurance companies on February 29, March 1, March 2, March 5, and March 9, 2004, with a total cumulative insurance amount of up to RMB 1,738,000. It can be determined that Huang Guoji failed to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure regarding the above inquiries made by the insurer. The fact that Huang Guoji had previously worked as a part-time agent for personal life insurance business at Taikang Life Insurance Co., Ltd. means that he should have had a more comprehensive and clear understanding of the duty of truthful disclosure than an ordinary policyholder, and should have had some understanding of matters to be noted in insurance risk control. Additionally, Huang Guoji's multiple insurance purchases were concentrated between February 29 and March 9, 2004, not long before the insurance application involved, making it impossible for him to have forgotten. Accordingly, it can be determined that Huang Guoji's failure to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure was intentional.

II. On the issue of whether the defendants Foshan Branch and Shunde Sub-branch should bear insurance liability.

First, both the plaintiff and the defendants confirmed that the salesperson Yan Xiaohui, who handled the insurance business involved, was a salesperson of the defendant Shunde Sub-branch. Yan Xiaohui's handling of the involved insurance business was an act performed in the course of employment. The corresponding legal liability arising from such an act in the course of employment should be borne by her employer, Shunde Sub-branch. Given that the branch of China Life Insurance Co., Ltd. in Foshan City is the defendant Foshan Branch, and Shunde Sub-branch is a subordinate unit of Foshan Branch without the capacity to independently issue insurance contracts in its own name or assume corresponding legal liability, the insurance contracts involved should be determined to have been concluded between Foshan Branch and Huang Guoji, and the resulting legal consequences should be borne by Foshan Branch.

Secondly, as previously discussed, when the applicant Huang Guoji purchased the "Xianghe Term Life Insurance" from the defendant, Foshan Branch, he intentionally violated his duty of truthful disclosure by failing to truthfully answer questions regarding whether he had applied for similar insurance from multiple insurance companies. The various insurances that Huang Guoji repeatedly applied for, including the insurance in question, were all types with low premiums and high payouts. The number of repeated applications was high, and the cumulative insurance amount reached as high as RMB 1,738,000. The corresponding insurance premiums were also a huge amount relative to Huang Guoji's annual income of RMB 50,000. The existence of the above circumstances created a significant potential moral hazard for the applicant. The applicant's failure to truthfully inform the insurer of the above circumstances directly affected the insurer's assessment of the applicant's personal risk and was sufficient to influence the insurer's correct decision on whether to underwrite the policy, how to determine the underwriting conditions and premium rates, etc. Therefore, the Foshan Branch's rescission of the "Xianghe Term Life Insurance Contract" signed with Huang Guoji, its refusal to pay compensation or insurance benefits for the insured event that occurred before the rescission of the insurance contract, and its refusal to return the insurance premium have factual and legal grounds. The plaintiff, He Lihong's, request for the Foshan Branch to pay insurance compensation based on the "Xianghe Term Life Insurance Contract" is not supported.

Thirdly, when the applicant Huang Guoji applied for the "Personal Accident Comprehensive Insurance" from the defendant, Foshan Branch, he neither filled in "Yes" nor "No" for Question 11 in Part Three of the application form regarding whether he had applied for insurance from multiple insurance companies, i.e., he did not answer. This also constitutes an intentional violation of the duty of truthful disclosure. The Foshan Branch, knowing of the existence of the above circumstance, neither made further inquiries to the applicant nor explicitly required the applicant to answer truthfully. Instead, it signed the "Personal Accident Comprehensive Insurance Contract" in question with the applicant and collected the premium. Although an insurer may rescind the insurance contract and refuse to bear compensation liability on the grounds that the applicant failed to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure, if the insurer, knowing that the applicant has not fulfilled the duty of truthful disclosure, does not require the applicant to disclose truthfully but instead enters into the insurance contract, it should be deemed to have voluntarily waived its right to defense. The above conduct of the Foshan Branch constitutes a voluntary waiver of the right to require the applicant to make truthful disclosure, forming a legally binding waiver, and therefore it is no longer entitled to assert the right to defense on this matter. Consequently, the Foshan Branch has no right to rescind the "Personal Accident Comprehensive Insurance Contract" (Contract No. 2004-441406-D31-58001682-5) signed with Huang Guoji. As the insured under this contract, Huang Guoji, has died in a traffic accident, and the insured event stipulated in the contract has occurred, the Foshan Branch shall pay the accident insurance compensation of RMB 300,000 to the beneficiary, the plaintiff He Lihong, in accordance with the contract.

In summary, in accordance with Article 6 and Article 107 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 5, Article 10, and Article 17 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China, Paragraph 1 of Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Item (7) of Article 40 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Item (1) of Article 70 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, the People's Court of Shunde District, Foshan City, on July 29, 2005, rendered the following judgment:

1. The defendant, Foshan Branch, shall, within ten days from the date the judgment takes legal effect, pay the plaintiff, He Lihong, insurance benefits of RMB 300,000 and interest (calculated at the同类 loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China, from November 22, 2004, until the date of payment);
2. The plaintiff, He Lihong's, other claims are dismissed.

The case acceptance fee is RMB 10,010, of which the defendant, Foshan Branch, shall bear RMB 6,670, and the plaintiff, He Lihong, shall bear RMB 3,340.

He Lihong, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Foshan Intermediate People's Court. Her main grounds for appeal were: 1. The appellee, Foshan Branch, signed the "Personal Accident Comprehensive Insurance Contract" with Huang Guoji first. Therefore, when signing the "Xianghe Term Life Insurance Contract" with Huang Guoji, it should have been clear that Huang Guoji had already applied for "Personal Accident Comprehensive Insurance," i.e., it should have been aware that Huang Guoji had participated in other personal insurance. However, the Foshan Branch still filled in "No" in Item 11 of the "Xianghe Term Life Insurance Contract," did not make any annotation in Item 12 regarding Huang Guoji's purchase of "Personal Accident Comprehensive Insurance," and did not raise any objection when reviewing the policy; instead, it issued the policy effective. The above conduct of the Foshan Branch indicates that, in signing the "Xianghe Term Life Insurance Contract" with Huang Guoji, it waived its right to defense on whether Huang Guoji had truthfully disclosed his repeated insurance applications. Therefore, the "Xianghe Term Life Insurance Contract" signed between the parties is lawful and valid, and the Foshan Branch should fulfill its contractual obligations and bear the liability for claims settlement. 2. The first-instance judgment erred in finding that the applicant Huang Guoji constituted "intentional failure to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure." According to the relevant provisions of the Insurance Law, for property insurance, notification to each insurer is required for double insurance, but for personal insurance, there is no explicit legal provision on whether notification to each insurer is required for repeated insurance. In other words, personal insurance can be repeatedly applied for multiple times. In reality, it is common for a person to purchase multiple personal insurance policies. Whether an applicant has repeated insurance does not affect the insurer's decision on whether to underwrite the policy. Therefore, the Foshan Branch's refusal to bear insurance liability on the grounds that Huang Guoji intentionally failed to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure is improper. The Foshan Branch had suspected He Lihong of insurance fraud and reported the case to the public security organ. After investigation, the Shunde Branch of the Foshan Public Security Bureau issued a "Notice of Decision Not to File a Case," fundamentally denying the possibility of fraud by He Lihong and Huang Guoji. However, even though there was sufficient evidence proving that He Lihong and Huang Guoji had no fraudulent intent, the first-instance court still subjectively assumed the possibility of fraud, which is unfair. In this case, whether the applicant truthfully disclosed the existence of repeated insurance was not the fundamental cause of the insured event in question. Therefore, even if it were a negligent failure to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure, it would not be sufficient to exempt the Foshan Branch from its insurance claims liability. In summary, she requested the court of second instance to set aside the first-instance judgment and instead order the appellees, Shunde Branch and Foshan Branch, to immediately pay He Lihong insurance benefits of RMB 500,000 and interest (calculated at the同类 loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period, from the date of filing the lawsuit until the date of payment), and to order the Shunde Branch and Foshan Branch to bear the costs of both the first and second instances.

The appellant, He Lihong, did not submit new evidence.

The appellees, Shunde Branch and Foshan Branch, argued in their defense: 1. The phrase "the applicant has already participated in or is applying for other personal insurance" refers to the applicant participating in or applying for insurance from other insurance companies, not to the applicant's multiple applications within the same insurance company. The appellant, He Lihong, intentionally made a distorted interpretation. The scope of the applicant's duty of truthful disclosure is conditional upon the insurer making an inquiry and the insurer not knowing the information. The applicant's participation in or application for insurance from other insurance companies is information unknown to the insurer. Whether the insurer is willing to underwrite a specific risk, and how to determine the premium amount to charge the applicant, depends on the insurer's correct estimation and judgment of the specific risk. Making a correct estimation can only be based on the applicant's statements, primarily on the applicant's answers to the "disclosure items" established by the insurer. The main purpose of establishing "disclosure items" is to facilitate the insurer's underwriting review. The insurer is, of course, aware of the applicant's past insurance history with it, so it would not make inquiries about this. What the insurer needs to know is the applicant's insurance history with other insurance companies. In this case, the applicant Huang Guoji and He Lihong both had experience in the insurance industry and had received relevant insurance knowledge training. They should have been aware of the scope of the disclosure items. 2. Even if He Lihong's interpretation were accepted, it could only be considered that the appellant waived its right to defense regarding the applicant's failure to truthfully disclose repeated insurance within the company. It cannot be inferred that the appellant waived its right to defense, based on the applicant's failure to truthfully disclose repeated insurance in other insurance companies, to rescind the insurance contract. In the absence of the applicant's truthful disclosure of records of repeated insurance in other insurance companies, it cannot be determined that the appellant's agreement to underwrite the insurance in question was a genuine expression of intent. 3. The first-instance judgment's finding that the applicant in question "intentionally failed to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure" was an objective assessment based on the facts of the case, not a "subjective assumption." The case facts show that the applicant in question indeed posed a significant moral hazard. Additionally, when the applicant applied for the "Xianghe Term Life Insurance" in question, in addition to requiring him to fill out the application form, the insurer also required him to fill out a "High Amount Financial Questionnaire," which again inquired about any other repeated insurance. The insurer's conduct fully reflects its high regard for the applicant's other insurance records. However, when filling out the questionnaire, the applicant again indicated that he had no other personal insurance. This shows that the applicant's failure to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure was not due to negligence but was intentional. 4. The applicant indeed failed to truthfully disclose his occupation, and the appellant has the right to rescind the insurance contract based on this. The first-instance judgment erred in its finding on this point. When applying for insurance, the applicant claimed to be the person in charge of "Lunjiao Construction Water and Electricity Installation Team" and "Shunji Water and Electricity Decoration." Based on this, the appellant classified the applicant's occupational risk as Class 1, with a premium rate of one per thousand. However, based on the appellant's investigation during the litigation, "Lunjiao Construction Water and Electricity Installation Team" and "Shunji Water and Electricity Decoration" do not exist at all. At the time of application, the applicant had no work unit and was a person without fixed occupation. The premium rate should have been three per thousand. According to Paragraph 2 of Article 17 of the Insurance Law, the insurer has the right to rescind the two insurance contracts in question. Furthermore, the applicant intentionally concealed his medical history. According to the appellant's knowledge, as early as 1985 during a physical examination, the Shunde Lunjiao Hospital diagnosed the applicant as "HbsAg" positive (hepatitis B virus carrier). In 2004, an examination at the First People's Hospital of Shunde found that the applicant was positive for four out of six hepatitis B tests, i.e., "HBeAg negative, anti-HBe positive, anti-HBc positive" (often referred to as "小三阳"). The applicant should have been aware of this but made false statements to the appellant, seriously affecting the appellant's proper underwriting review. The appellant also has the right to rescind the insurance contracts in question based on this. The first-instance judgment ordering the Foshan Branch to pay He Lihong interest on the personal accident insurance benefits has no factual or legal basis. 5. The Shunde Branch does not have the capacity to issue insurance contracts or assume insurance liability in its own name. The first-instance court correctly dismissed He Lihong's claims against the Shunde Branch, and this should be upheld. In summary, He Lihong's grounds for appeal are clearly untenable. The appellee requests the court of second instance to conduct a comprehensive review of the case and dismiss all of He Lihong's claims.

During the second instance, the appellee, Foshan Branch, submitted one medical record from the former Shunde County Lunjiao Health Center (1985) and one inpatient diagnosis medical record from the First People's Hospital of Shunde (2004). These were submitted to prove that the applicant Huang Guoji intentionally concealed the fact that he was a hepatitis B virus carrier.

The Foshan Intermediate People's Lawfully organized the parties to cross-examine the evidence. Regarding the evidence submitted by the appellee, Foshan Branch, in the second instance, the appellant, He Lihong, argued: 1. The evidence submitted by the Foshan Branch was formed before the first-instance lawsuit, but the Foshan Branch did not submit it. Therefore, it does not constitute new evidence, and she refused to cross-examine it; 2. She disputed the authenticity of the above evidence. The 1985 medical record from the former Shunde County Lunjiao Health Center bore the disease certificate seal of Shunde County Lunjiao Health Center, and the 2004 inpatient diagnosis medical record from the First People's Hospital of Shunde bore the seal of the Medical Affairs Department of the First People's Hospital of Shunde. Neither is an official seal, so their authenticity cannot be determined; 3. The Foshan Branch never stated that an applicant carrying the hepatitis B virus cannot purchase personal insurance, nor did it inform the applicant of the disclaimer on this matter. Moreover, the above evidence does not clearly show that Huang Guoji was a hepatitis B virus carrier. The court of second instance held that: The scope of the applicant's duty of truthful disclosure should be limited to matters that the applicant knew or should have known at the time of applying for insurance. The diagnostic date of the 2004 inpatient diagnosis medical record from the First People's Hospital of Shunde, submitted by the Foshan Branch, was after Huang Guoji signed the insurance contracts in question with the Foshan Branch. Therefore, it cannot prove that Huang Guoji intentionally failed to truthfully disclose his medical condition at the time of application. Based on the content of the 1985 medical record from the former Shunde County Lunjiao Health Center, submitted by the Foshan Branch, the reason Huang Guoji visited the former Shunde County Lunjiao Health Center at that time was abdominal pain, and the tests performed were not specific hepatitis B tests. Huang Guoji was not a medical professional and could not have known that he was a hepatitis B virus carrier based on the conclusion from the blood test at that time showing HbsAg positive. Therefore, he could not have informed the Foshan Branch of this fact when applying for insurance. The Foshan Branch had no other evidence to prove that Huang Guoji knew or should have known that he was a hepatitis B virus carrier at the time of applying for the insurance in question. Relying solely on the above evidence to claim that Huang Guoji intentionally concealed his hepatitis B medical history is insufficient. In summary, the evidence submitted by the Foshan Branch in the second instance was not admitted.

Upon the second instance trial, the Foshan Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first instance and additionally found the following: When Huang Guoji applied for the insurance in question, the appellee, Foshan Branch, issued him the "High Amount Financial Questionnaire," requiring him to truthfully fill in information regarding his insurance history, work situation, personal assets, liabilities, etc. Under the "Insurance History" column in the questionnaire, there were sub-items for "Insurance Date," "Insurance Company," "Insurance Amount," etc. At the top of the questionnaire, there was a boldfaced important notice column stating: "The following information is only used to assess the insured amount required by the insured. Our company will strictly maintain client confidentiality." At the end of the questionnaire, there was a similarly boldfaced applicant/insured declaration column stating: "I have understood all requirements of this questionnaire, and all information filled in is true and accurate. All the above statements and this declaration will become the basis for issuing the policy and, together with the application form, will form part of the insurance contract." When Huang Guoji applied for the "Personal Accident Comprehensive Insurance" in question, he filled out the aforementioned "High Amount Financial Questionnaire," but made no entries in the insurance history column.

The Foshan Intermediate People's Court held in the second instance: The appellant, He Lihong, did not appeal against the first-instance judgment regarding the "Personal Accident Comprehensive Insurance Contract." Although the appellee, Foshan Branch, raised objections to this in its defense in the second instance, it did not file a formal, lawful appeal. In accordance with Articles 35 and 36 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on the Reform of Civil and Economic Trial Methods, the court of second instance will not review or handle the disputes between the parties concerning this insurance contract.

The issues in dispute in the second instance are: 1. Whether Huang Guoji fulfilled his duty of truthful disclosure when applying for the "Xianghe Term Life Insurance" in question; 2. If Huang Guoji did not fulfill his duty of truthful disclosure when applying for the "Xianghe Term Life Insurance" in question, whether the appellee, Foshan Branch, has the right to rescind the insurance contract based on this and refuse to bear insurance liability.

The Foshan Intermediate People's Court held in the second instance:

1. Concerning the issue of whether Huang Guoji fulfilled his duty of truthful disclosure when applying for the "Xianghe Term Life Insurance" in question.

An insurance contract is an aleatory contract. Whether the insurer underwrites the risk and how it determines the premium depend on the insurer's correct estimation and judgment of the insured risk. The applicant's truthful disclosure of relevant matters is an important basis for the insurer to correctly determine the insurance risk and take control measures. According to the principle of good faith, the applicant must truthfully disclose, based on what he knows or should know, any matters inquired about by the insurer on the application form or risk questionnaire. In this case, when Huang Guoji applied for the "Xianghe Term Life Insurance" in question, the appellee, Foshan Branch, inquired about his insurance history. However, Huang Guoji concealed the actual situation of his multiple repeated insurance applications with other insurance companies and gave an answer that was clearly inconsistent with the facts. This obviously violated the legal duty of truthful disclosure. The first-instance court, considering the intensive timing of Huang Guoji's repeated insurance applications and his specific background as a part-time insurance agent, correctly found that Huang Guoji intentionally failed to fulfill his duty of disclosure. This finding is appropriate and should be upheld.

2. Concerning the issue of whether, given that Huang Guoji did not fulfill his duty of truthful disclosure when applying for the "Xianghe Term Life Insurance" in question, the appellee, Foshan Branch, has the right to rescind the insurance contract based on this and refuse to bear insurance liability.

Whether an insurer can rescind an insurance contract and refuse to bear insurance liability due to an applicant's failure to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure should be determined by whether the matters not truthfully disclosed by the applicant were sufficient to affect the insurer's correct decision on whether to underwrite the policy and how to determine the underwriting conditions and premium rates. This determination cannot be based on the subjective perception of the applicant, insured, beneficiary, or insurer. It must be based on an objective and comprehensive assessment of the specific content and nature of the matters not truthfully disclosed, taking into account various circumstances. According to the actual situation in the insurance industry, whether an applicant has already participated in or is applying for other personal insurance is an important basis for the insurer to correctly assess the underwriting risk and decide whether to underwrite the policy and how to determine the underwriting conditions and premium rates. An applicant's failure to truthfully disclose the above matters will directly affect the insurer's correct assessment and decision-making and is sufficient to affect the conclusion of the insurance contract. Based on the facts of this case, the appellee, Foshan Branch, inquired through the application form and the "High Amount Financial Questionnaire" whether the applicant, Huang Guoji, had already participated in or was applying for other personal insurance. However, Huang Guoji did not answer truthfully, violating his duty of truthful disclosure. As the insurer, the Foshan Branch has the right, in accordance with Article 17, Paragraph 2 of the Insurance Law, which states: "If the applicant intentionally conceals facts and fails to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure, or negligently fails to fulfill the duty of truthful disclosure, and such failure is sufficient to affect the insurer's decision on whether to agree to underwrite the policy or to increase the premium rate, the insurer has the right to rescind the insurance contract," to rescind the "Xianghe Term Life Insurance Contract" signed with Huang Guoji, and to refuse to pay compensation or insurance benefits for the insured event that occurred before the rescission of the insurance contract, and also not to return the insurance premium. The appellant, He Lihong, as the beneficiary, has no legal basis for requesting the Foshan Branch to bear insurance liability under this insurance contract. Her corresponding claims are not supported by law.

In summary, the first-instance judgment has clear findings of fact, correct application of law, and lawful trial procedures, and should be upheld. In accordance with Item (1) of Paragraph 1 of Article 153 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Foshan Intermediate People's Court, on January 10, 2006, rendered the following judgment:

Appeal dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee is RMB 10,010, to be borne by the appellant, He Lihong.

This judgment is final.
